_comment: Same legal text as eu-ai-act@2026-1744: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 AS AMENDED by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of 8 July 2026 (consolidated text 02024R1689-20260727). This is a REVISION of that lens, not a new amendment, and it exists for ADR-0101 (accepted 2026-10-23). The 2026-1744 lens was cut for the Annex IV file of a high-risk provider: it said nothing of the system's qualification nor of Articles 4, 5, 14 and 50, Art. 50 lived only in `notes`, and no renderer printed `notes`, so a reader could take that silence for an absence of obligation. This revision adds operator-required rows for them -- runward supplies nothing for any of them, the rows only make their absence visible -- and sets `printNotes`, so the draft prints the dated notes under its header. No primary text was re-read for it: every date below is carried over from eu-ai-act@2026-1744. The identifier `2026-1744-r2` sorts after `2026-1744` (src/lib/regimes.ts: lexicographic, highest = default); eu-ai-act@2026-1744 stays shipped, selectable with --regime-version, and renders as before. An amendment or a further revision is a NEW regimes/eu-ai-act@<version>.json, never an edit of this file (ADR-0022).
label: EU AI Act (Annex IV)

source._comment: `reviewBy` is a CALENDAR guess, not a change detector, and the gap is measurable: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 was published on 24 July 2026 while this sheet's predecessor expired on 2 August, so it was wrong for nine days before the alarm could ring. `consolidatedSeen` is the actual state of the source: the watch fetches `url`, takes the highest identifier matching `consolidatedPattern`, and compares. A newer one is a HARD signal that the text moved, independent of any date we guessed.

notes: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (OJ L, 12 July 2024) as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of 8 July 2026 (OJ L, 2026/1744, 24.7.2026), in force 27 July 2026. Chapter III Sections 1-3 -- and ONLY those, Section 5 is not named by Art. 113(3)(c) and its fate is not established -- apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III, Art. 6(2)) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I, Art. 6(1)). Governance (Chapter VII) has applied since 2 August 2025, NOT 2026: what moved to 2 August 2026 on the GPAI side is Art. 101 (fines on general-purpose model providers). Art. 50 transparency applies from 2 August 2026, with Art. 111(4) giving pre-2 August 2026 synthetic-content systems until 2 December 2026. New prohibited practices (Art. 5(1)(ba),(bb) and 5(1a),(1b)) apply 2 December 2026. Art. 11(1) as replaced lets SMEs and SMCs use a simplified technical documentation form the Commission must establish; no deadline is set, and notified bodies must accept it. This lens (2026-1744-r2, 23 October 2026, ADR-0101) adds operator-required rows for the system's qualification and Articles 4, 5, 14 and 50; it re-reads no primary text, and every date in these notes is carried over from eu-ai-act@2026-1744.

highRisk.scope: Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3 -- Art. 113, 3rd para, point (c), as replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. Annex III systems (Art. 6(2)) from 2 December 2027; Annex I systems (Art. 6(1)) from 2 August 2028.

annexIv.supplies: **architecture, validation procedures + metrics, cybersecurity (manifest + rubric + threat model); design choices, alternatives, assumptions, pre-determined changes = the ADR journal**
annexIv.provider: third-party sourcing/licensing, sign-off on test logs

annexIv.supplies: accuracy characterization, input-data specs, oversight tooling

operatorRequired: **System qualification** — record it first, it decides which of the rows below bind: is the system high-risk under Annex III (art. 6(2)) or Annex I (art. 6(1))? Is it an **art. 50** case (an AI system interacting with natural persons, generating synthetic content, used for emotion recognition or biometric categorisation, or generating deep fakes)? Does it involve a prohibited practice of **art. 5** (the new ones, art. 5(1)(ba),(bb) and 5(1a),(1b), apply from 2 December 2026)? runward does not determine this; a blank here is not a "no".
**Art. 4 AI literacy** — the AI literacy measures you take, and their record.

**Art. 14 human oversight** — your human oversight measures. Binding only for a **high-risk** system, from the high-risk dates in this draft's header; the oversight tooling listed under Point 3 is an input to them, not the measures.

**Art. 50 transparency** — the measures for each art. 50 case your qualification identifies. Art. 50 applies from **2 August 2026**, with art. 111(4) giving pre-2 August 2026 synthetic-content systems until **2 December 2026**. runward does not observe what a running system discloses to the persons it reaches.
**Point 1** general description (intended purpose, provider, versioning) · **Point 5** RMS governance & risk acceptance (art. 9).

**Point 7** harmonised-standards selection · **Point 8** the signed **EU declaration of conformity** (art. 47) · **Point 9** the **post-market monitoring plan** (art. 72(3); the Commission must adopt guidance and a template by 2 September 2027).
**Art. 12 runtime event logs** — produced by the running system, not by runward.
disclaimerTail: Annex IV wording moves — confirm against the Official Journal (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689) before filing.
